High level answers up front:
- "Responses" and "Chat completions" are charged on token usage but the way tokens are attributed differs slightly (prompt vs completion attribution, and some historical meters have been consolidated on the backend).
- Function call args and streamed partial outputs are included in token counts; we'll show explicit examples below.
- Legacy meters (we sometimes call them legacy-chat or legacy-completions) map to new rate card lines; we can provide a one-to-one mapping table and sample invoice rows.

We'll follow up with a concrete 2-row sample invoice that maps to your CSV. Expect that in the next message from Rishi.

Hi Alex — summarizing with concrete examples mapped to invoice rows. I used the sample you attached (thanks) and created two representative requests: a short-turn bot (many small replies) and a function-call pattern.

Example A — short-turn chat (Chat Completions endpoint):
- Request: single-turn chat with a 40-token prompt, model produces a 90-token completion.
- Billing: billed as 130 tokens total. On the invoice you'll see a line like:
  "Hosted API | model=gpt-4o-hosted | endpoint=chat.complete | tokens=130 | unit_price=$0.0006 | amount=$0.078"

Example B — function call (Responses endpoint, streaming):
- Request: prompt + function args = 180 tokens; model streams a 320-token completion in 8 chunks.
- Billing: prompt+args counted as 180 prompt tokens; streamed output counted as 320 completion tokens -> 500 tokens billed total. Each streamed chunk does not create a separate invoice line — we aggregate per request. Invoice row example:
  "Hosted API | model=gpt-4o-hosted | endpoint=responses | tokens=500 | unit_price=$0.00055 | amount=$0.275"

Notes & differences:
- Unit prices can differ per endpoint family and model. In the examples above I used $0.0006 for chat.complete and $0.00055 for responses as illustrative only; actual tiered unit prices for your committed rates will be in the rate card.
- Function call arguments, whether passed as JSON attributes or inserted inline, are treated as part of the prompt token count. The function's returned JSON is counted as completion/output tokens.
- Legacy meters (legacy-chat, legacy-response) are mapped in the billing backend to the current endpoint names; we will include a mapping table in the PDF ratecard we attached. For accounting you can treat legacy lines as equivalent to the new endpoint lines once we provide the mapping.

Attached is a 2-row mock invoice (see pdf and CSV attachment) generated from your sample for quick reconciliation. If you prefer, we can also include both token columns (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) in exported CSVs so your finance system gets granular rows.
